s: Which one of the following correctly describes the constitutional arrangement under Article 268?
o: The Union levies and collects the tax, but distributes it exclusively to local bodies
The States levy, collect and appropriate the tax
The Union levies the tax and the States collect and appropriate it
The States levy the tax and the Union collects and appropriates it
x: Article 268 covers duties levied by the Union but collected and appropriated by the States. Stamp duties on bills of exchange, cheques and promissory notes are examples.
tq: Match the constitutional article with the correct authority exercising levy and collection powers.
sec: Tax levy, collection, appropriation - Articles 268, 269, 270 and classification  [APPSC]

s: Which of the following is an example of a duty covered under Article 268?
o: Tax on agricultural income
Tax on inter-State supply under IGST
Surcharge on Union taxes
Stamp duty on bills of exchange and cheques
x: Stamp duties on bills of exchange, cheques and promissory notes are levied by the Union but collected and appropriated by the States under Article 268.
tq: Use the example attached to the article rather than relying only on the article number.
sec: Tax levy, collection, appropriation - Articles 268, 269, 270 and classification  [APPSC]

s:
Consider the following statements regarding Article 268A:
1. It was inserted by the 88th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003.
2. It dealt with service tax collected by both the Union and the States.
3. It was omitted by the 101st Constitutional Amendment Act.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
x: Article 268A was introduced by the 88th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003, for service tax collected by the Union and the States, and was omitted after the 101st Constitutional Amendment Act.
tq: Check the amendment sequence and the subject of the omitted constitutional provision.
sec: Tax levy, collection, appropriation - Articles 268, 269, 270 and classification  [APPSC]

s: Tax on inter-State sale or purchase and consignment of goods was constitutionally associated with which Article?
o: Article 269
Article 270
Article 268
Article 282
x: Article 269 dealt with taxes on inter-State sale or purchase and consignment of goods. These taxes were levied and collected by the Union and assigned to the States.
tq: Distinguish between Union taxes shared under Article 270 and taxes assigned to States under Article 269.
sec: Tax levy, collection, appropriation - Articles 268, 269, 270 and classification  [APPSC]

s: With reference to Article 269A, which one of the following is correct?
o: It deals with surcharge collected wholly by the Union
It deals with State excise duty on liquor
It deals with taxes on professions and callings
It deals with IGST on inter-State supply
x: Article 269A concerns IGST on inter-State supply. The proceeds are apportioned between the Centre and the States on the advice of the GST Council.
tq: Separate the similar-looking Articles 269 and 269A by identifying the specific GST subject.
sec: Tax levy, collection, appropriation - Articles 268, 269, 270 and classification  [APPSC]

s: The proceeds of IGST on inter-State supply are apportioned between the Centre and the States on the advice of the:
o: GST Council
Inter-State Council
Finance Commission
Comptroller and Auditor General of India
x: Article 269A provides for apportionment of IGST on inter-State supply between the Centre and the States on the advice of the GST Council.
tq: Identify the constitutional body associated with the specific tax-distribution mechanism.
sec: Tax levy, collection, appropriation - Articles 268, 269, 270 and classification  [APPSC]

s: Which of the following correctly describes the taxes covered by Article 270?
o: All Union List taxes without any exceptions
Union List taxes shared through the Finance Commission, excluding specified taxes, surcharges and cesses
Only customs duties and Union excise duties
All State List taxes collected by the Union
x: Article 270 covers Union List taxes shared as recommended by the Finance Commission, but excludes Articles 268, 269 and 269A taxes, Article 271 surcharges and cesses.
tq: Watch for the extreme word “all” and test the constitutional exclusions from the divisible pool.
sec: Tax levy, collection, appropriation - Articles 268, 269, 270 and classification  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the authority that levies it?
o: Customs duty — State Government
Agricultural income tax — Union Government
Excise on liquor — State Government
Entertainment tax — Union Government exclusively
x: Excise on liquor is a State tax. Customs duty is levied by the Union, agricultural income tax by the States, and entertainment tax is largely subsumed in GST except for local bodies.
tq: Use the “who levies the tax?” test to distinguish Union and State revenue sources.
sec: Tax levy, collection, appropriation - Articles 268, 269, 270 and classification  [APPSC]

s: Which of the following statements regarding the 80th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2000, is correct?
o: It introduced an alternative scheme of devolution based on pooling and sharing all Union taxes
It abolished the Finance Commission
It transferred all customs revenue to the States
It introduced GST with effect from 1 April 1996
x: The 80th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2000, effective from 1 April 1996, introduced an alternative scheme of devolution under which all Union taxes were pooled and shared, replacing the earlier arrangement involving 29% of certain taxes.
tq: Connect the amendment number with its distinctive devolution change and effective date.
sec: Tax levy, collection, appropriation - Articles 268, 269, 270 and classification  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Article 265 — Taxes may be imposed without statutory authority in emergencies
Article 271 — Surcharge on specified Union taxes for the Union
Article 276 — Finance Commission and its recommendations
Article 293 — Borrowing by the Union
x: Article 271 deals with surcharges on taxes referred to in Articles 269 and 270, and the proceeds are wholly for the Union. Article 265 requires authority of law for taxation, Article 276 concerns professional taxes, and Article 293 concerns State borrowing.
tq: Start from the sure article-function pair and eliminate reversals of nearby article numbers.

s: Which Article is associated with grants in lieu of export duty on jute and jute products to Assam, Bihar, West Bengal and Odisha?
o: Article 275
Article 282
Article 293
Article 273
x: Article 273 provided grants in lieu of export duty on jute and jute products to Assam, Bihar, West Bengal and Odisha.
tq: Discriminate between the two nearby grant provisions by the specific beneficiary States and purpose.

s: The constitutional ceiling on taxes on professions, trades, callings and employments under Article 276 is:
x: Article 276 concerns taxes on professions, trades, callings and employments, subject to a ceiling of ₹2,500.
tq: Use the exact statutory ceiling and distinguish it from nearby round-value distractors.

s:
Which one of the following correctly represents the pairing of constitutional Articles and subjects?
1. Article 280 — Finance Commission
2. Article 281 — Recommendations of the Finance Commission laid before Parliament
3. Article 285 — Exemption of Union property from State taxation
4. Article 289 — Exemption of State property from Union taxation
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
o: 1 and 2 only
1, 2 and 3 only
2, 3 and 4 only
x: All four pairings are correct. Articles 280 and 281 concern the Finance Commission and its recommendations, while Articles 285 and 289 concern reciprocal tax immunities of Union and State property.
tq: Verify each article against its neighbouring constitutional subject before selecting the complete combination.

s: Which of the following correctly distinguishes Articles 292 and 293?
o: Article 292 concerns grants and Article 293 concerns taxation
Article 292 concerns Union borrowing, whereas Article 293 concerns State borrowing
Article 292 concerns State borrowing, whereas Article 293 concerns Union borrowing
Both Articles concern borrowing by local bodies
x: Article 292 deals with borrowing by the Union, while Article 293 deals with borrowing by the States.
tq: Discriminate between adjacent article numbers by assigning the Union provision first and the State provision second.

s: Which statement regarding tax immunities is correct?
o: State goods are always exempt from customs and excise duties
Central corporations are automatically immune from all State taxes
The Centre cannot tax a State’s commercial operations under any circumstance
Central corporations are separate legal entities and are not immune from State taxes merely for being Central corporations
x: Central corporations are separate legal entities and do not enjoy automatic immunity from State taxes. The Centre may also tax a State’s commercial operations and levy customs or excise on State goods.
tq: Reject absolute immunity claims and distinguish constitutional immunity of government property from separate legal entities.

s: The divisible pool of Central taxes is calculated by deducting which of the following from gross tax revenue?
o: Cesses, surcharges and cost of collection
States’ share and Finance Commission grants
All taxes collected under Article 270
Only customs duties and Union excise
x: The divisible pool is gross tax revenue minus cesses, surcharges and the cost of collection. The net proceeds are certified by the Comptroller and Auditor General.
tq: Apply the formula by identifying the deductions rather than the items included in the pool.

s: Who certifies the net proceeds relevant to the divisible pool?
o: Union Finance Ministry
GST Council
Finance Commission
Comptroller and Auditor General of India
x: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India certifies the net proceeds used in determining the divisible pool.
tq: Use the institutional-responsibility approach: identify who certifies rather than who recommends devolution.

s:
Which of the following is included in the divisible pool of Central taxes?
1. Personal income tax
2. Centre’s share of IGST
3. Customs
4. Union excise
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
o: 1 and 2 only
1, 2 and 3 only
2, 3 and 4 only
x: Personal income tax, the Centre’s share of IGST, customs and Union excise are included in the divisible pool. The pool also includes corporation tax and CGST.
tq: Test inclusions collectively and avoid confusing included Union taxes with excluded cesses and surcharges.

s: Which one of the following is excluded from the divisible pool?
o: Customs duty
Personal income tax
A surcharge under Article 271
Union excise duty
x: Surcharges under Article 271 are excluded from the divisible pool. Article 268 and 269 taxes and cesses for specific purposes are also excluded.
tq: Find the excluded item among ordinary divisible-pool tax receipts.

s: What percentage of the divisible pool was recommended as the States’ share for 2021–26 and retained for 2026–31?
x: The States’ share was fixed at 41% of the divisible pool for 2021–26 by the Fifteenth Finance Commission and retained by the Sixteenth Finance Commission for 2026–31.
tq: Distinguish the headline percentage share from the lower effective share of gross tax revenue.

s: Why are cesses and surcharges generally not shared with the States through the divisible pool?
o: They are collected by local bodies
Article 270 excludes them from the taxes shared with the States
The Finance Commission has no constitutional existence
They are levied only by State legislatures
x: Cesses and surcharges remain outside the divisible pool because Article 270 excludes them from the taxes shared with the States. Article 271 surcharges are specifically for the Union.
tq: Link the fiscal consequence to the precise constitutional exclusion.
sec: Cesses and surcharges - share and why outside the pool

s: Which of the following were identified as examples of cesses used by the Centre?
o: Finance Commission Cess, GST Cess, and Borrowing Cess
Krishi Kalyan Cess, Health and Education Cess, and fuel or road cess
Jute Export Cess, Profession Cess, and Local Body Cess
Agricultural Income Cess, Customs Cess, and State Excise Cess
x: Krishi Kalyan Cess, Health and Education Cess, and fuel or road cess are examples of cesses referred to in the context of the Centre’s shift towards cesses.
tq: Recognise the named examples and reject invented combinations using familiar tax terminology.
sec: Cesses and surcharges - share and why outside the pool

s: The amount of cesses and surcharges per ₹100 of Central tax was at a decade high in which year and at what level?
x: Cesses and surcharges amounted to ₹13.5 per ₹100 of Central tax in 2021–22, described as a decade high. The estimate for 2025–26 was ₹11.
tq: Keep the year-value pair intact and avoid swapping the historical figure with the estimate.
sec: Cesses and surcharges - share and why outside the pool

s:
Arrange the following periods in descending order of the divisible pool as a percentage of gross tax revenue:
A. FC-15 period
B. FC-13 period
C. FC-14 period
Select the correct sequence.
o: B, C, A
A, C, B
C, B, A
B, A, C
x: The divisible pool declined from 89.2% during the FC-13 period to 82.1% during FC-14 and 78.3% during FC-15. Therefore, the descending order is FC-13, FC-14 and FC-15.
tq: Compare the numerical trend first, then arrange the periods rather than relying on the numerical order of FC labels.
sec: Cesses and surcharges - share and why outside the pool

s: Which of the following correctly represents the reported trend in the divisible pool as a percentage of gross tax revenue?
o: 78.3% during FC-13, 82.1% during FC-14 and 89.2% during FC-15
89.2% during FC-13, 78.3% during FC-14 and 82.1% during FC-15
89.2% during FC-13, 82.1% during FC-14 and 78.3% during FC-15
82.1% during FC-13, 89.2% during FC-14 and 78.3% during FC-15
x: The divisible pool’s share of gross tax revenue fell from 89.2% in the FC-13 period to 82.1% in FC-14 and 78.3% in FC-15.
tq: Track the direction of the percentage trend before matching each figure to its period.
sec: Cesses and surcharges - share and why outside the pool

s: The divisible pool was approximately what percentage of gross tax revenue in 2025–26?
x: The divisible pool was approximately 81% of gross tax revenue in 2025–26.
tq: Separate the current estimate from the earlier FC-period percentages.
sec: Cesses and surcharges - share and why outside the pool

s: What was the approximate effective devolution to the States as a percentage of gross tax revenue, despite the headline 41% share of the divisible pool?
x: Because cesses and surcharges are outside the divisible pool, the effective devolution was approximately 30–32% of gross tax revenue, lower than the headline 41% of the divisible pool.
tq: Distinguish a percentage of the divisible pool from a percentage of gross tax revenue.
sec: Cesses and surcharges - share and why outside the pool

s: Which statement best captures the difference between the headline and actual share of States in total tax receipts?
o: States receive approximately 41% of total tax receipts without adjustment
States receive no share in Union tax receipts
States’ share in total tax receipts is approximately 34%, although the headline divisible-pool share is 41%
States’ share in total tax receipts is approximately 50% because cesses are included
x: The States’ share in total tax receipts was approximately 34%, while 41% is the headline share of the divisible pool. The difference results largely from cesses and surcharges remaining outside the pool.
tq: Identify the denominator before comparing two apparently different devolution percentages.
sec: Cesses and surcharges - share and why outside the pool

s: Which of the following was cited as the Centre’s defence regarding expenditure of cess collections?
o: All cess collections were transferred directly to the Finance Commission
The Centre spent 50% of cess collections on States over six years
Over six years, the Centre spent 105% of cess collections on States
The Constitution prohibits cesses but permits surcharges
x: The Centre’s defence was that the Constitution permits cesses and that, over six years, it spent 105% of cess collections on the States.
tq: Test the stated justification separately from the criticism of cesses.
sec: Cesses and surcharges - share and why outside the pool

s: What was the central feature of the ‘grand bargain’ associated with the Sixteenth Finance Commission?
o: States would accept a smaller share of a larger pool if most cesses were merged into regular taxes
States would surrender all Finance Commission grants
The Centre would abolish all forms of indirect taxation
States would receive a larger share of a smaller pool if all cesses were retained
x: The proposed grand bargain involved States accepting a smaller percentage share of a larger pool if the Centre merged most cesses into regular taxes.
tq: Translate the policy proposal into its two linked conditions: pool size and percentage share.
sec: Cesses and surcharges - share and why outside the pool

s: Which one of the following statements about the debate on cesses is correct?
o: The Punchhi Commission abolished Article 271
The Sixteenth Finance Commission recommended a binding cap on all cesses
The Sixteenth Finance Commission made no recommendation on capping cesses, while the 5% cap was attributed to the Punchhi Commission
The Finance Commission has no role in discussing cesses
x: The Sixteenth Finance Commission was criticised for not recommending a cap on cesses. The reference to a 5% cap was attributed to the Punchhi Commission.
tq: Separate the recommendation actually made from the recommendation attributed to another commission.
sec: Cesses and surcharges - share and why outside the pool

s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes Article 275 grants from Article 282 grants?
o: Article 275 grants are available to any State without reference to need
Article 275 grants are discretionary and Article 282 grants are statutory
Article 275 grants are recommended by the Finance Commission, whereas Article 282 grants are discretionary grants for any public purpose
Both are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India
x: Article 275 provides statutory grants-in-aid recommended by the Finance Commission. Article 282 permits discretionary grants by the Union or State executive for any public purpose.
tq: Compare the recommending authority and legal character before considering the beneficiaries.

s:
Which of the following is a beneficiary or purpose specifically associated with Article 275 grants?
1. States in need
2. Welfare of Scheduled Tribes
3. Administration of Scheduled Areas
4. Any public purpose selected by the executive
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
o: 1 and 2 only
1, 2 and 3 only
2, 3 and 4 only
x: Article 275 grants are for States in need and include grants for Scheduled Tribe welfare and Scheduled Areas. Grants for any public purpose selected by the executive are associated with Article 282.
tq: Separate the constitutional beneficiaries of statutory grants from the broad purpose of discretionary grants.

s: Which statement regarding the source of charge or vote is correct?
o: Article 275 grants are voted, whereas Article 282 grants are charged
Article 275 grants are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India, whereas Article 282 grants are voted
Both Article 275 and Article 282 grants are charged
Neither type of grant is reflected in parliamentary financial procedure
x: Article 275 statutory grants are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India, whereas Article 282 discretionary grants are voted.
tq: Use the charged-versus-voted distinction to separate the two grant provisions.

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with Article 282 grants?
o: Recommended exclusively by the Finance Commission and limited to Scheduled Areas
Made by the Union or State executive for any public purpose and used for Centrally Sponsored Schemes
Charged on the Consolidated Fund of India and restricted to States in need
Available only for welfare of Scheduled Tribes
x: Article 282 grants are discretionary grants made by the Union or State executive for any public purpose and have been used for Centrally Sponsored Schemes.
tq: Identify the broad purpose and executive character of Article 282 before eliminating statutory-grant features.

s: Which criticism has been associated with Article 282 discretionary grants?
o: They are constitutionally impossible after the abolition of the Planning Commission
They are always smaller than Article 275 grants
They may be politically motivated and bypass the Finance Commission
They can be given only to Scheduled Areas
x: Article 282 grants have been criticised as potentially politically motivated and as bypassing the Finance Commission.
tq: Test the critical evaluation attached to the constitutional provision, not merely its definition.

s: Which development followed the abolition of the Planning Commission in 2015?
o: Statutory grants under Article 275 were abolished
Plan grants ended
Article 282 was deleted
The Finance Commission ceased to recommend grants
x: With the Planning Commission abolished in 2015, plan grants ended. Article 275 statutory grants and Article 282 discretionary grants continued as distinct constitutional categories.
tq: Connect the institutional change with the specific category of grants that ended.

s: Under Article 292 of the Constitution, the Union Government may borrow:
o: On the security of the Consolidated Fund of India within limits fixed by Parliament
On the security of the State Consolidated Funds with the consent of State legislatures
Only from the Reserve Bank of India without any statutory limit
Only after obtaining the consent of the Finance Commission
x: Article 292 permits the Union to borrow on the security of the Consolidated Fund of India, subject to limits fixed by Parliament.
tq: Identify the constitutional authority and security attached to the borrowing power.

s:
Consider the following statements regarding borrowing by States under Article 293:
1. States may borrow within India on the security of their Consolidated Funds.
2. A State requires the Centre's consent to borrow if it owes any loan to the Centre.
3. The Centre may lend to or guarantee loans raised by States.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
x: All three statements correctly describe the borrowing provisions under Article 293.
tq: Check each statement against the constitutional conditions attached to State borrowing.

s: A State Government that has an outstanding loan from the Union Government proposes to raise a fresh loan within India. Which constitutional requirement becomes relevant?
o: It cannot borrow under any circumstances
It must obtain the consent of every other State
It must obtain prior approval from the Comptroller and Auditor General
It must obtain the consent of the Centre
x: Under Article 293, a State indebted to the Centre cannot borrow without the Centre's consent. The Constitution does not impose an absolute prohibition on such borrowing.
tq: Apply the conditional restriction rather than treating the power as an absolute prohibition.

s: Which one of the following is associated with the recommendations of the Sixteenth Finance Commission regarding State finances?
o: A fiscal deficit ceiling of 3% of GDP for the Union alone
A fiscal deficit ceiling of 5% of GSDP and expansion of off-budget borrowing
A fiscal deficit ceiling of 3% of GSDP and ending off-budget borrowing
A prohibition on all State borrowing from domestic sources
x: The Sixteenth Finance Commission caps the State fiscal deficit at 3% of GSDP and calls for ending off-budget borrowing.
tq: Match the numerical ceiling with the correct level of government and fiscal practice.

s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding constitutional funds.
List-I (Fund)
 a. Consolidated Fund
 b. Public Account
 c. Contingency Fund
List-II (Article)
 i. Article 267
 ii. Article 266(2)
 iii. Article 266(1)

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
o: a–iii, b–ii, c–i
a–ii, b–iii, c–i
a–iii, b–i, c–ii
a–i, b–ii, c–iii
x: The Consolidated Fund is covered by Article 266(1), the Public Account by Article 266(2), and the Contingency Fund by Article 267.
tq: Start from the sure constitutional article and eliminate codes with a misplaced fund.
sec: Consolidated Fund, Contingency Fund, Public Account

s: Which of the following correctly describes withdrawal from the Consolidated Fund of India or a State?
o: It is governed by the rules of the Public Account
It requires only the recommendation of the Finance Commission
It requires an appropriation law under Article 114(3)
It can be made by executive order without legislative authority
x: Withdrawal from the Consolidated Fund requires an appropriation law, with Article 114(3) applying to the Union appropriation process.
tq: Distinguish legislative appropriation from executive access to public funds.
sec: Consolidated Fund, Contingency Fund, Public Account

s:
Consider the following statements about the Public Account:
1. It is referred to in Article 266(2).
2. Parliamentary authorisation is not required for withdrawals from it.
3. The Government acts as a trustee in respect of amounts such as provident funds, small savings and deposits.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
x: All three statements correctly describe the Public Account, including its constitutional basis, withdrawal arrangement and trustee character of government.
tq: Use the distinction between ownership or trusteeship of funds and parliamentary appropriation.
sec: Consolidated Fund, Contingency Fund, Public Account

s: Which one of the following is the correct feature of the Contingency Fund?
o: It is governed by Article 292 and is used only for State borrowings
It is governed by Article 267 and permits advances by the executive, which are recouped later
It is governed by Article 266(2) and requires prior Parliamentary authorisation for every advance
It is part of the Public Account and cannot be replenished
x: The Contingency Fund is provided under Article 267. Advances may be made by the executive and are recouped later.
tq: Discriminate between the fund's article and its executive advance mechanism.
sec: Consolidated Fund, Contingency Fund, Public Account

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Public Account — Withdrawal only after appropriation under Article 114(3)
Contingency Fund — Advances by the executive, recouped later
Public Account — Government acts as trustee
Consolidated Fund — Withdrawal only by appropriation law
x: The Public Account does not require Parliamentary authorisation for withdrawal. The appropriation requirement under Article 114(3) relates to withdrawal from the Consolidated Fund.
tq: Find the fund whose withdrawal rule has been deliberately swapped with another fund.
sec: Consolidated Fund, Contingency Fund, Public Account

s: The Rajamannar Committee was set up in:
x: The Rajamannar Committee was set up in 1969 by the Tamil Nadu Government.
tq: Test a specific year against the nearby years of other Centre-State commissions.

s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Rajamannar Committee?
o: It was set up to establish the Inter-State Council in 1990
It was set up by the Tamil Nadu Government and advocated greater State autonomy and more resources
It was set up by the Union Government to recommend a cap on cesses
It was set up to recommend a 3% fiscal deficit limit for States
x: The Rajamannar Committee was constituted by the Tamil Nadu Government in 1969 and argued for greater State autonomy and more resources.
tq: Use the setter–committee–recommendation combination rather than a year alone.

s:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I (Commission or Committee)
 a. Rajamannar Committee
 b. Sarkaria Commission
 c. Punchhi Commission
List-II (Period or year)
 i. 1969
 ii. 1983–1988
 iii. 2007–2010

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
o: a–i, b–ii, c–iii
a–ii, b–iii, c–i
a–iii, b–i, c–ii
a–i, b–iii, c–ii
x: The Rajamannar Committee dates to 1969, the Sarkaria Commission to 1983–1988, and the Punchhi Commission to 2007–2010.
tq: Match each body to its period, beginning with the distinctive single-year entry.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Sarkaria Commission was set up by the Union.
2. Its recommendations led to the establishment of the Inter-State Council under Article 263 in 1990.
3. The Punchhi Commission was set up by the Tamil Nadu Government.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the Punchhi Commission was set up by the Union, not the Tamil Nadu Government.
tq: Catch the wrong constituting authority while retaining the correct institutional consequence.

s: Which of the following was associated with the Punchhi Commission?
o: A proposal to abolish the Inter-State Council under Article 263
A recommendation that States should have no own revenue
A cap on cesses at 5% and time-bound disposal of bills
A ceiling of 3% on the Union's fiscal deficit
x: The Punchhi Commission is associated with a 5% cap on cesses and time-bound disposal of bills.
tq: Link the commission to its distinctive percentage and institutional recommendation.

s: P.V. Rajamannar also served as the Chairman of the:
o: Fourth Finance Commission
Second Finance Commission
Sarkaria Commission
Punchhi Commission
x: P.V. Rajamannar also chaired the Fourth Finance Commission.
tq: Separate a person's role in a committee on Centre-State relations from the person's Finance Commission role.

s: Which of the following best explains vertical fiscal imbalance in India?
o: States possess larger and more buoyant tax bases while the Union bears most expenditure responsibilities
States have no constitutional expenditure responsibilities
The Union possesses larger and more buoyant tax bases, while States bear major responsibilities such as health, education, agriculture and police
Both the Union and States have identical tax bases and expenditure responsibilities
x: Vertical fiscal imbalance arises because the Union controls larger and more buoyant tax bases, including corporate tax, income tax and most GST, while States undertake major public services.
tq: Compare revenue capacity with expenditure responsibility at the two levels of government.

s:
Which of the following factors aggravate vertical fiscal imbalance?
1. Cesses and surcharges
2. Loss of independent indirect taxes to GST
3. Conditionalities attached to Centrally Sponsored Schemes
4. Weak own revenue of States
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
o: 1 and 2 only
1, 2 and 3 only
2, 3 and 4 only
x: Cesses and surcharges, the loss of independent indirect taxes after GST, CSS conditionalities and weak own revenue all aggravate the imbalance.
tq: Recognise the cumulative fiscal causes rather than selecting only the tax-related factors.

s: According to the stated budget figures, total transfers to States in 2026–27 amounted to:
o: ₹30.14 lakh crore
₹25.44 lakh crore
₹27.44 lakh crore
₹22.74 lakh crore
x: Total transfers to States in 2026–27 were stated as ₹25.44 lakh crore, which was ₹2.7 lakh crore higher than in 2025–26.
tq: Use the exact budget amount and distinguish it from the stated year-on-year increase.

s: The increase in total transfers to States from 2025–26 to 2026–27 was stated to be:
o: ₹2.7 lakh crore
₹3.6 lakh crore
₹1.2 lakh crore
₹2.0 lakh crore
x: The increase was ₹2.7 lakh crore, taking total transfers to ₹25.44 lakh crore in 2026–27.
tq: Separate the absolute increase from the CSS component mentioned separately.

s: In the budgeted rise from 2025–26 Revised Estimates to 2026–27 Budget Estimates, approximately what share was attributed to Centrally Sponsored Scheme revenue transfers?
x: The budgeted rise was 12.2%, of which about 42%, or ₹1.2 lakh crore, was attributed to CSS revenue transfers.
tq: Match the percentage share with the correct base and the CSS component.

s: The Tamil Nadu Assembly resolution of August 2026 was related to the demand for:
o: Transfer of police to the Union List
Fair tax devolution
Abolition of all State borrowing limits
Replacement of GST by corporation tax
x: The Tamil Nadu Assembly resolution demanded fair tax devolution, making it a current Centre-State fiscal issue.
tq: Identify the specific fiscal demand rather than an unrelated constitutional reform.

s: The expression “41% illusion” refers to the criticism that:
o: The Centre rejected all recommendations of the Sixteenth Finance Commission
The Centre accepted Finance Commission devolution but deferred structural fiscal reforms
Cesses were fixed permanently at 41% of gross tax revenue
States received 41% of total government expenditure as grants
x: The criticism is that the Centre accepted the Finance Commission's devolution figure while deferring deeper structural fiscal reforms.
tq: Interpret the slogan through the policy criticism attached to it, not through a literal percentage calculation.

s: Which of the following forms part of Andhra Pradesh's grants and borrowing-related fiscal arrangements?
o: Only corporation tax transfers and foreign currency loans
Revenue Deficit Grants under Article 292 and SDLs through the Finance Commission
Revenue Deficit Grants under Article 275, CSS funds, local body grants and SDLs through the RBI
Only local body grants, with no role for Centrally Sponsored Schemes
x: Andhra Pradesh's fiscal arrangements include Revenue Deficit Grants under Article 275, Centrally Sponsored Scheme funds, local body grants and State Development Loans through the RBI.
tq: Combine the State-specific grant sources with the correct constitutional article and borrowing channel.

s: Which one of the following is NOT a responsibility listed among the major expenditure responsibilities of States in the context of vertical fiscal imbalance?
o: Agriculture
Monetary policy
Health
Education
x: Health, education and agriculture are listed as major State responsibilities. Monetary policy is not listed as a State expenditure responsibility.
tq: Find the item outside the stated group of State service responsibilities.
